hook: Match claims to four experts debating free museum entry by tracking each person's stance, not their keywords.
intro: Four statements on one question — should museums abolish admission charges? — from a cultural economist (A, Vogt: the audience stays the same, invest in outreach), a museum director (B, Aydin: first-time visitors doubled, revenue offset), a cultural journalist (C, Sölle: the price is secondary, content matters) and a head of culture (D, Reinhardt: fees fund restoration, a middle way). The task gives eight paraphrased claims and asks "Wer äußert das?". All four talk about money, visitors and families, so shared words prove nothing: the stance and the exact function of each sentence decide. First write a three-word summary per expert, then match each claim to a summary.
tips[0].title: Summarise each expert before reading the claims
tips[0].text: A: Publikum bleibt gleich → Vermittlung. B: eigene Erfahrung, Erstbesucher verdoppelt → Ausgleich. C: Preis zweitrangig → Inhalte. D: Einnahmen nötig → Mittelweg. With these in hand, the claims become look-ups.
tips[0].check.why: The price is dismissed and the quality of the exhibitions blamed, so the core stance is: content matters more than the price.
tips[1].title: Match the stance, not a shared word
tips[1].text: Families appear in B and D, money in all four. "Wer nennt Wege, fehlende Einnahmen zu ersetzen?" is B (how to replace them), not D (what they are used for). "Wer hält den Preis für nebensächlich?" is only C, although everyone mentions the price.
tips[1].trap: Two experts can touch the same topic from opposite ends; the claim's verb (ersetzen vs verwenden, beschränken vs abschaffen) tells you which one.
tips[1].check.why: Both lines talk about money, but the claim asks what the money is used for (verwenden), not how missing money is replaced (ersetzen).
tips[1].visual.right: the expert says it like this
tips[1].visual.rows[0].b: Die Kosten stehen in keinem Verhältnis zum Nutzen.
tips[2].title: Learn the paraphrase pairs
tips[2].text: nebensächlich = zweitrangig · ausgleichen = ersetzen / kompensieren · Erstbesucher = Menschen, die zum ersten Mal kommen · Vermittlung = Bildungsarbeit · ohnehin kulturaffin = gehen sowieso ins Museum · langweilig geworden = Qualität des Angebots. The claims are paraphrases, never quotations.
tips[2].check.why: ohnehin = sowieso, and regelmäßig gehen = Stammbesucher sein; the claim says the same thing in different words.
remember[0]: Three-word summary per expert first; then match each claim to a stance.
remember[1]: Shared words are traps: the verb of the claim (ersetzen, beschränken, verwenden) decides.
exam: Matching claims to the expert who made them is a typical C1 exam reading task — and how you read any debate page.
